author: Afloat16
title: fix: count all provider replies toward Agent token budgets
body:
### Related Issues

No existing issue. Reproduced on main at `4b4346b6d798338d9b43e70115006494012b1756`.

### Proposed Changes:

An Agent using `FallbackChatGenerator` can receive usage dictionaries from different providers in successive steps. If one reply reports `total_tokens` and another reports only input/output counts, the accumulated total contains only the first reply. For example, two 100-token replies leave `total_tokens` at 100, so a budget of 150 incorrectly allows a third LLM call. Switching between input/output key conventions without explicit totals has the same problem.

- Derive a missing total from each reply's input/output counts before accumulating usage.
- Preserve provider-reported numeric totals, including zero and totals containing thinking tokens.
- Leave the original reply metadata and nested usage details unchanged.
- Document the derived total and add a release note.

### How did you test it?

[Fork validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/haystack/actions/runs/43665680621):
- Restored the base implementation while keeping the new tests: all six sync/async fallback regressions fail because the Agent incorrectly exits with `text`.
- Restored the fix and ran the complete budget-hook, Agent utility, Agent, and fallback-generator unit test modules: 238 passed; 4 integration tests deselected.
- Scoped `hatch run fmt-check`, `hatch run test:types`, release-note generation with Reno, and the repository's pre-commit checks: all passed.

The regressions use the real `Agent`, `FallbackChatGenerator`, tool execution, and `MockChatGenerator` response functions. They cover both orders of replies with/without totals and a switch between input/output key conventions. No external model API is called.

### Notes for the reviewer

The implementation and regression tests were generated with an AI assistant.

### Checklist

- I have read the [contributors guidelines](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [code of conduct](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/main/code_of_conduct.txt).
- Related issue update: not applicable; no existing issue.
- I have added unit tests and updated the docstrings.
- I have used a conventional `fix:` title.
- I have documented the behavior and added a release note.
- I have run the repository's pre-commit hooks in the linked fork CI.
